final:
STATUS: pass

SUMMARY: I ran 20 probes across the criteria and the hostile inputs, plus the overlays suite. None reproduced a failure of an acceptance criterion. The one surprise, a moved target that leaves its old wrapper visible, matches how the light-DOM path already behaves, so I'm treating it as minor. Probe files are deleted and `git status` matches the start (the same four modified files).

FILES TOUCHED: none (probe files were created under packages/@react-aria/overlays/test/ and deleted; git status unchanged)

FINDINGS:
- [minor] Moving the target itself out of a wrapper inside a shadow root leaves the now-empty wrapper unhidden. Nothing re-walks the old container when a target leaves it. The light-DOM code has the same gap, but I did not run HEAD to confirm. Not a criterion.
- [minor] Light-DOM children of a path host (slotted content) get hidden when appended later. Consistent with the initial walk, so arguably intended, but worth a look if slotted targets are common.

CHECKS:
- `yarn jest packages/@react-aria/overlays` → pass (10 suites, 201 tests)
- P1 sibling host with inner elements: only host hidden, inner untouched, all restored → pass
- P2 announcer inside a sibling host present before the call: announcer and its wrapper visible → pass
- P3 target moved to a shadow sibling position: target visible, moved node is the target itself → fail on my expectation that the old wrapper gets hidden (see minor finding); the target-stays-visible part passed
- P4 role=row in shadow root with cell inside: row and cell hidden, restored → pass
- P5 host with shadow content appended into enclosing shadow root: host hidden, inner not → pass
- P6 same as P5 but in light body → pass
- P7 two calls, second targets in another shadow root, first reverted first: sibling in B still hidden, late content in B hidden, all restored → pass
- P8 custom root inside shadow root: outside root untouched, inside siblings hidden, later additions hidden → pass
- P9 revert after host removed from document: no throw, light sibling restored → pass
- P10 keepVisible in shadow root: kept element not hidden → pass
- P11 announcer added to sibling host shadow after call: not hidden → pass
- P12 pre-existing aria-hidden sibling in shadow root kept after revert → pass
- P13 light child of a path host hidden, host itself visible → pass
- Q1 child moved out of target into shadow sibling position: hidden, target visible, restored → pass
- Q2 target host as target: later shadow content visible, light sibling hidden, restored → pass
- Q3 same shadow root, two calls, out-of-order revert, refcounts → pass
- Q4 deep descendant appended inside target stays visible → pass
- Q5 host removed between late addition and revert → pass
- R1 siblings after a hidden host and after the path host, in shadow and light DOM, all hidden; host's inner content untouched; restored → pass
- Not run: flag-off probe with the flag never enabled; the existing flag-off test already covers that. Inert path probed only by the existing test.

OPEN QUESTIONS: Should a target that leaves its container re-hide that container (the P3 minor)? Light DOM behaves the same, so I'd lean to leave it.
